title: Weekly Allowance
learning_objectives: Decide between spending now and saving for later

events.description: It's Week 1! You get $10 allowance. Your friend invites you to the movies ($8) and there's a book fair at school ($5). What do you want to do?

choices.label: Go to the movies
choices.effect: You saw an awesome movie! You have $2 left this week.

choices.label: Shop at the book fair
choices.effect: You got a great book! You have $5 left this week.

choices.label: Save it all
choices.effect: You put $10 in your savings! Great patience!

events.description: Week 2! Another $10 allowance. There's a cool toy you've been wanting for $20. You also need art supplies for school ($6).

choices.label: Buy art supplies
choices.effect: You got everything you need for art class! Nice planning!

choices.label: Save toward the toy
choices.effect: You're getting closer to that toy! Great saving!

choices.label: Buy supplies and save the rest
choices.effect: Supplies bought and $4 saved! You're balancing needs and wants!

events.description: Week 3! Another $10. A friend is having a birthday and you want to get them a gift ($7). There's also a bake sale ($3).

choices.label: Buy a birthday gift
choices.effect: Your friend will love this gift! You have $3 left.

choices.label: Gift ($7) and bake sale ($3)
choices.effect: Gift AND cupcakes! You spent your whole allowance but made great memories!

choices.label: Make a homemade gift, save money
choices.effect: A handmade gift from the heart! And you saved all $10!

events.description: Week 4! Last week of the month. Let's count up your savings and see what you've accomplished!

choices.label: Buy something fun with savings
choices.effect: You earned a treat! Saving up feels rewarding!

choices.label: Keep saving for next month
choices.effect: Look at those savings grow! You're building great habits!

recap_template: You managed your allowance for a whole month! You practiced deciding between spending, saving, and giving. Every choice taught you something about budgeting.
positive_framing_rules: Never say the student wasted money
Celebrate both spending and saving as valid strategies
Frame gift-giving as a positive use of money
ai_variation_allowed: Change the specific items available to buy

title: Bake Sale Business
learning_objectives: Understand that making things costs money
Set prices for items you sell
Track money coming in and going out

events.description: You're running a bake sale! You have $20 to buy ingredients. Cupcake mix costs $8 (makes 12 cupcakes) and cookie dough costs $5 (makes 20 cookies). What do you buy?

choices.label: Cupcakes ($8) and cookies ($5)
choices.effect: Great variety! You spent $13 and have $7 left. You have 12 cupcakes and 20 cookies to sell!

choices.label: Two batches of cupcakes ($16)
choices.effect: 24 cupcakes ready to sell! You spent $16 and have $4 left.

choices.label: Four batches of cookies ($20)
choices.effect: 80 cookies! That's a LOT of cookies to sell! You spent all $20.

events.description: Time to set your prices! How much will you charge?

choices.label: $1 each — sell a lot!
choices.effect: Low prices attract lots of customers! Nearly everything sold!

choices.label: $2 each — balanced
choices.effect: Good price! Most items sold and you earned more per item!

choices.label: $3 each — earn more per item
choices.effect: Higher prices! Fewer people bought, but you earned more from each sale!

events.description: The bake sale is going great! A teacher asks if you can donate some for the school raffle. What do you do?

choices.label: Donate 5 items
choices.effect: That's so generous! The teacher thanks you and tells everyone about your stand!

choices.label: Keep selling everything
choices.effect: You focus on your business and earn more money! Smart business thinking!

recap_template: You ran a bake sale business! You learned about buying ingredients, setting prices, and making decisions about your earnings. Great job, entrepreneur!
positive_framing_rules: Never say the student priced things wrong
Celebrate both generous and business-minded choices
Frame all outcomes as learning experiences
ai_variation_allowed: Add weather or surprise customer events

title: Pet Care Budget
learning_objectives: Understand ongoing costs vs one-time costs
Plan a budget for taking care of a pet
Make choices about wants vs needs for a pet

events.description: You're adopting a puppy! You have $50 to get started. First, your puppy needs food and a bowl. Dog food is $15 and a bowl is $5. What else do you want to get?

choices.label: Food ($15) + Bowl ($5) + Toy ($8)
choices.effect: Food, bowl, and a squeaky toy! Your puppy is so happy! $22 left.

choices.label: Food ($15) + Bowl ($5) + Bed ($20)
choices.effect: Food, bowl, and a cozy bed! Your puppy has a place to sleep! $10 left.

choices.label: Just food ($15) + Bowl ($5)
choices.effect: The essentials are covered! You have $30 left for other things!

events.description: Your puppy needs a vet visit for a checkup. It costs $25. Do you have enough?

choices.label: Take puppy to the vet
choices.effect: Your puppy got a clean bill of health! Taking care of your pet is important!

choices.label: Save up more first
choices.effect: You'll save up for the vet visit. Let's plan when you can go!

events.description: Your puppy chewed up their toy! A new toy costs $8, but your friend has a gently used one for $3.

choices.label: Buy a brand new toy
choices.effect: A shiny new toy! Your puppy loves it!

choices.label: Get the used toy from your friend
choices.effect: Your puppy doesn't care if it's used — they love it! And you saved $5!

choices.label: Make a toy from old socks
choices.effect: Your puppy thinks the sock toy is the best thing ever! Creative and free!

recap_template: You learned how to budget for a pet! Pets need food, vet visits, and toys — some costs happen once and others come back again and again.
positive_framing_rules: Never say the student is unable to care for their pet
Frame budget limits as planning opportunities
Celebrate creative solutions like DIY toys

title: Garage Sale

events.description: You're having a garage sale! You found old toys, books, and games to sell. First, you need to set prices. How do you price your old board game?

choices.label: $5 — it's in great shape!
choices.effect: A fair price! It takes a while but someone buys it for $5!

choices.label: $2 — sell it fast!
choices.effect: It sold right away! Quick sale for $2!

choices.label: $4 but willing to go lower
choices.effect: A customer offers $3 and you agree! Nice negotiating!

events.description: A kid your age comes by and really wants your old bike. You were thinking $15. They only have $10.

choices.label: Sell it for $10
choices.effect: The kid is thrilled! $10 is still great earnings!

choices.label: Wait for someone who'll pay $15
choices.effect: Later, an adult buys it for $15! Patience paid off!

choices.label: Trade for their skateboard + $5
choices.effect: A trade and some cash! Creative deal-making!

events.description: The sale is almost over. You have a few items left. A neighbor offers to buy everything remaining for $8 total.

choices.label: Take the $8 deal
choices.effect: Everything sold! Your table is clear and you earned $8 more!

choices.label: Donate the rest
choices.effect: You donate the leftovers to a charity shop. So generous!

events.description: Time to count your earnings! What do you want to do with the money you made?

choices.label: Save half, spend half
choices.effect: A balanced plan! Some for fun now and some for later!

choices.label: Save it all for something big
choices.effect: All saved! You're on your way to something awesome!

choices.label: Buy something fun right away
choices.effect: You treated yourself! You earned it!

recap_template: You ran a garage sale! You set prices, negotiated with customers, and decided what to do with your earnings. Great business skills!
positive_framing_rules: Never say the student priced things wrong
